title: Full-round fixed-target key collisions for AES
summary: Determine whether full-round AES-128, AES-192, or AES-256 admits a sub-birthday fixed-zero-plaintext key collision attack.

formal_statement.body: For each $\ell\in\{128,192,256\}$, decide whether there are distinct AES-$\ell$ keys $k_1,k_2$ such that $\operatorname{AES}_{k_1}(0)=\operatorname{AES}_{k_2}(0)$ using fewer than approximately $2^{64}$ trials in the AES-GCM padding-fix key-commitment setting. A reduced-round or free-target collision does not settle the full-round fixed-zero-plaintext question.

scope.domain: Full-round AES key collisions for fixed-target plaintext in authenticated-encryption key commitment
assumptions: The plaintext is the fixed all-zero block
AES key length is 128, 192, or 256 bits
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source provides only reduced-round fixed-target attacks: 2-round AES-128, 5-round AES-192, and 6-round AES-256. No inspected later result gives a sub-2^64 full-round fixed-zero-plaintext collision or an impossibility proof.
